title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1971-12-01

ai_review.summary: Matrix blend captures a blazing 45‑minute set with a monster The Other One and soaring Jerry, delivered in crystal‑clear sound.
ai_review.review: The partial second set from December 1971 is hailed as one of the band’s most elemental performances – tight, psychedelic jams and an on‑fire The Other One that drives the crowd wild.  The matrix mix expertly fuses board clarity with audience ambience, giving listeners a vivid “you are there” experience despite occasional comments about the tape sounding fast.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of detailed reviews praise both the musical performance and the matrix recording quality, yielding a strong combined score despite a few outlier low‑star comments.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, raw mix that blends soundboard fidelity with audience ambience; many note crisp separation and powerful “you are there” feel. One reviewer mentioned the playback feels a bit fast, but overall the recording is considered superb.

standout_songs: Going Down the Road Feeling Bad
Too (The Other One) – especially the X‑factor jam around 6:00
show_quality.setlist_flow: A partial second set of roughly 45 minutes that builds from a tight, ethereal jam into a relentless first half of The Other One, then rolls through NFA > GDTRFB > NFA with textbook precision.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as “flying at supersonic speeds,” taking the band on fire and delivering a massive solo in The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: Called a “monster” and “wicked loud,” providing relentless, powerful bass throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: One reviewer wonders if the piano/keyboard is Keith or Tom Constanten; another notes Keith being “left in the dust.”
